deliverable: A source-grounded summary of what two Bilibili knowledge videos say - video A (科学科普) on whether smelling a bad smell counts as eating it, and video B on the week-long 'fish bloom' of AI comment bots on Bilibili - with per-segment ASR locators, explicit gaps where the captions are unintelligible, and no frame- or slide-level claims.

turns.text: Using only these two captured ASR transcripts, summarize what each video says: in video A, what the speaker claims about inhaling odour molecules, the kissing comparison, and his explanation for why the smell is judged foul; in video B, how he reconstructs the timeline of the 'fish bloom', what the originating plugin did, and how the 2.0 update tried to stop it. Attribute each point to video A or video B and give the ASR segment locator.

Video A only: what does the speaker say about the mass of odour molecules a sniff carries, about what kissing would imply if smelling counted as eating, and about where the foulness is decided? Stay within the sentences the ASR makes intelligible, flag garbled tokens instead of repairing them, and do not discuss the sponsored product segment as if it were the video's evidence.

Video B only: why, in the speaker's account, did the 2.0 'no public comments' change fail to reduce the bots, what did the author himself report, and what safety advice does the speaker give viewers? Keep to the captured transcript, do not describe any frames or slides, and mark garbled product names as unclear rather than guessing them.

acceptable_partial_outcomes: The transcripts are ASR only: no frames, slides, on-screen text, thumbnails or comments were inspected, and video A's transcript stops at 2:58 of a 3:31 video, so its closing section is uncaptured.

The ASR is noisy and mixes Simplified and Traditional characters with homophone errors (臭 rendered as 抽, 粪便 as 奋辨, 鼻腔 as 逼腔); garbled personal names, product names, version numbers and the 2015-study details must be reported as unclear rather than repaired.

Video B's account of the NPM account suspension and the download statistics is the speaker's second-hand reconstruction; video A's sponsored segment (02:19 onward) describes a commercial product and is not an independent authority.

reference_review.method: quotes sliced from ASR snapshots and re-checked as literal substrings

authority_anchors.supports: NIDCD states that olfactory disorders involve the sense of smell and explains that smell molecules reach olfactory receptor cells in the nose which send signals to the brain, and that smell is linked to taste. Independent confirmation of the perception chain video A describes (molecules in, receptors, brain); it is not evidence for the speaker's own sentences.

The Cyberspace Administration of China's Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (2023) set out requirements for services that generate text and other content, including obligations on providers. Independent confirmation that AI-generated public content is a regulated activity, the premise behind video B's account of mass AI-written comments; it is not evidence for the speaker's own sentences.
